<!--
Use a conventional commit title in plain language, e.g. "fix(server): new threads no longer spike CPU".
Keep a PR to one underlying problem. Delete any section that genuinely does not apply.
-->

## Problem

<!-- The problem in a sentence or two: what is wrong, what was expected, and where it shows up. -->

## Change

<!-- How this fixes it. If it spans packages, say why one fix needs all of them. -->

## Upstream cost

<!-- GedCode is a fork that tracks T3 Code. Every upstream file this PR edits is a file that will
conflict on the next merge, so name them and justify each. "None — additive only" is the usual and
preferred answer. -->

## Verification

<!-- The focused tests and manual checks you actually ran, and what you observed. "Tests pass" alone
says nothing. Name anything you could not check.

For UI changes include before/after screenshots, and a short recording when timing or interaction
matters. Upload evidence to GitHub; never commit PR-only assets. -->

## Ged discipline

<!-- Who verified, and independently of whom. Paste the verdict record or link it. A change that
landed without an independent verifier's ruling should say so plainly rather than leave this blank. -->
